learningObjectives: Create and set customizable Application Settings using Configuration Sets
Organize Configuration Sets that associate Configuration settings with a common element
Reference Configuration settings using the Condition Builder

elements.description: A low-code framework for exposing selected application-behavior parameters. Use it to reduce hardcoded configuration and unnecessary Rule overrides; it does not eliminate every Rule change or guarantee an application has no defects.

A named group of Configuration settings for a specific feature or Case Type, created in App Studio. Rules (classes, Data Pages, properties) are auto-generated in Dev Studio. Name stored as pyLabel of a class Rule (max 64 chars).

elements.text: A settings panel separates a feature’s adjustable parameters from its implementation. Changing a guidance toggle is simpler than rewriting its visibility Rule each time. Access still matters: being a manager or user does not automatically grant permission to edit every setting.

elements.caption: A Configuration Set groups related settings tied to a feature or Case Type. Settings are referenced via the Condition Builder.

elements.description: For the application-behavior customization described in this lesson, Configuration settings are recommended in place of DSS. This is not evidence that all platform DSS records disappear or that every system setting should be migrated blindly.

bulletPoints: Expose selected configurable parameters and reduce unnecessary Rule overrides.
Configuration Set = named group of settings tied to a feature or Case Type.
Name stored as pyLabel of a class Rule — max 64 characters.
Settings are data instances of the Data-Configuration-Setting class.
Created in App Studio → underlying rules visible in Dev Studio.
Prefer Configuration settings for the described application-customization use case; do not infer removal of every DSS.

elements.description: Use App Studio → Settings → Configurations to develop the groups. Authorized users can customize exposed values at runtime without switching to design-time tools. A newly created Set appears on the landing page only after it contains a setting.
Three access roles for Configuration Sets and settings:
items: Administrators (PegaRULES:SysAdm4): Read/Write/Delete on both Configuration Sets and settings
Managers (PegaRULES:WorkMgr4): Read/Write/Delete on Sets, Read-only on individual settings
bulletPoints: Administrators can grant additional access to specific users or groups.

Administrators can update the access configuration.</text></g></svg>
elements.caption: These are role defaults, not immutable permissions or authority granted merely by a job title.

elements.description: Configuration Sets are defined in the Pega-Configuration class structure and included in the deployment file generated by product Rules. Configuration settings are included only when the 'Include associated data' checkbox is selected during product file creation.

bulletPoints: Navigate: App Studio → Settings tab → Configurations.
Admins: full Read/Write/Delete on Sets AND individual settings.
Managers: Read/Write/Delete on Sets; Read-only on individual settings.
Users: Read-only on both Sets and settings.
Deployment: must select 'Include associated data' during product file creation.
Runtime editing depends on the operator’s actual setting permissions.

elements.description: Reference Configuration settings throughout the application using the Condition Builder. The Condition Builder provides a menu to select a Configuration Set, then the specific setting within it. Allows business logic to react dynamically to setting values without hardcoding.

A guidance setting can control instruction visibility. An authorized operator changes the value after users adopt the Process. This avoids changing the Rule for that value adjustment; it is not a promise of instantaneous propagation to every open session.

bulletPoints: Reference via Condition Builder: select Set → select setting.
No hardcoded values — behavior driven dynamically by setting values.
Logic using the configured value can respond without a new Rule override; do not promise zero-latency refresh everywhere.

examPitfalls.title: Application customization recommendation is not global DSS removal
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Do not infer an exact introduction version or universal DSS deprecation from this lesson.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Use the recommended low-code Configuration settings for the described exposed application parameters. Review unrelated system settings separately.

examPitfalls.title: Configuration Set name max = 64 characters
examPitfalls.trapDescription: The documented name limit is 64 characters. Do not invent a particular save-error message from the length constraint.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: The Configuration Set name is stored as the pyLabel of a class Rule and has a maximum length of 64 characters.

examPitfalls.title: Managers can edit Sets but only READ individual settings (by default)
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Questions ask what access level Managers have for Configuration Settings. Candidates say 'full read/write.' By default, Managers can create and edit Configuration Sets but can only read individual setting values — editing individual values requires elevated permissions.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Managers (WorkMgr4) have Read/Write/Delete on Configuration Sets by default, but only Read access on individual Configuration settings. Admins can grant additional access.

examPitfalls.title: Users are Read-only — not runtime editors
examPitfalls.trapDescription: A question asks whether end users can change Configuration Setting values at runtime. Candidates say yes if the Set is published. End users have read-only access to Configuration Settings — only operators with appropriate access can modify values.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: User4 is read-only by default. WorkMgr4 also reads individual settings by default; setting-value changes require the applicable write permission, which administrators can grant.

examPitfalls.title: 'Include associated data' must be selected for deployment
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Questions ask how to deploy Configuration Settings to another environment. Candidates describe exporting rules only. When packaging for deployment, the 'Include associated data' option must be selected — otherwise the Configuration Setting values are not included in the package.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Configuration settings are only included in the deployment file when 'Include associated data' is explicitly selected during product file creation.

examPitfalls.title: Create Configuration Sets in App Studio — not Dev Studio
examPitfalls.trapDescription: A question asks where to create Configuration Sets. Candidates navigate to Dev Studio. Configuration Sets are created in App Studio under the Settings section — they are an App Studio citizen-developer-facing feature.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: The documented development surface is App Studio. Supporting generated Rules are visible in Dev Studio; this observation is not a universal ban on inspecting or editing all generated artifacts.

examPitfalls.title: Use the documented Condition Builder selection
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Do not turn the supported menu reference into a claim that every other technical access path is impossible.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: In Condition Builder, select the Configuration Set and setting. Verify any additional Rule-level access method against its own documentation.

quickRecap.value: Low-code framework for customizing app behavior without Rule overrides. Easier maintenance, faster upgrades, shorter time-to-market.
Named group of related settings tied to a feature or Case Type. Max 64-char name (stored as pyLabel of a class Rule). Created in App Studio.
Prefer Configuration settings for the application-customization use case described here; do not infer universal DSS removal.
SysAdm4 defaults: Read/Write/Delete on Sets and settings.
WorkMgr4 defaults: Read/Write/Delete Sets; Read settings. Broader access can be granted.
User4 defaults: Read Sets and settings. Actual access can be updated by an administrator.
App Studio → Settings tab → Configurations landing page.
Condition Builder → select Configuration Set → select specific setting.
Select 'Include associated data' during product file creation — not automatic.
